historical_claims.anchor: early research on generalized Schur functions and rational interpolation with Joseph Weiss and Vladimir Bolotnikov
At Cambridge he wrote a 2013 Part Three essay on applications of empirical process theory
completed a 2016 doctorate entitled Spectral Methods and Computational Trade-offs in High-Dimensional Statistical Inference
Richard Samworth was his doctoral supervisor
An early collaboration with Sébastien Bubeck and Nitin Viswanathan concerned multiple identifications in multi-armed bandits
a research fellowship at the Cantab Capital Institute for the Mathematics of Information in Cambridge
then a lectureship at University College London
He moved to the London School of Economics
the 2015 Biometrika paper A Useful Variant of the Davis–Kahan Theorem for Statisticians with Yi Yu and Richard Samworth
In 1972 Per-Åke Wedin developed influential singular-subspace perturbation bounds
Their rectangular extension performed an analogous service for singular subspaces
In a 2016 Annals of Statistics paper, Wang, Quentin Berthet and Richard Samworth investigated this trade-off
Under a widely used computational-hardness assumption associated with planted clique problems
Wang and Samworth's 2018 paper on high-dimensional change-point estimation via sparse projection
Their method, called inspect, uses a cumulative-sum transformation
Wang's 2022 work with Ziwei Zhu and Richard Samworth studied high-dimensional PCA with heterogeneous missingness
They proposed primePCA, an iterative procedure
In 2023 Wang wrote a short personal commentary for Harvard Data Science Review about the influence of Sir David Cox
In a 2022 paper with Feng Gao, Wang investigated two-sample testing
In 2023 the Royal Statistical Society awarded Wang the Guy Medal in Bronze
He also received the Society's Research Prize in 2019
